messages.author: b70e5a419fc15914
messages.subject: Choosing/formatting a reference panel
parts:
Hi Folks,

I'm attempting to munge some summary statistics.  I have no trouble when using the Hapmap 3 reference panel. However, using Hapmap results in the loss of about 17% of the SNPs (don't know if that's typical or not--this is an ancestrally diverse sample). Since I'm planning to do gSEM within the sample, all sumstats files have the same SNPs, so it seems preferable to not drop any SNPs in the munge process. 

I wrote my own reference panel file based on the sumstats, but using it results in the following error: 


munge(files=files, hm3=snplist, trait.names=trait_names, N=n_eff)
.
.
.
Merging file:sumstats.tab with the reference file:snplist.snplist
99 rows present in the full sumstats.tab summary statistics file.
0 rows were removed from the sumstats.tab summary statistics file as the rs-ids for these rows were not present in the reference file.
Error in `$<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, "effect", value = logical(0)) :
  replacement has 0 rows, data has 99

It seems this must be due to some error in my snplist file, as the process works fine with the HapMap SNPs.  What might the difference be?  Truncated sumstats and snplist and munge syntax are attached. 

Katherine

messages.author: b70e5a419fc15914
messages.subject: Re: Choosing/formatting a reference panel
parts: For the benefit of anyone looking to resolve this issue, I munged in LDSC and got useful error message, which indicated column headers in the .snplist file must be "SNP", "A1" and "A2". Variants like "ALLELE1" are acceptable in sumstats files, but not in snplist files.
